newsitem.title: FRANCE: SAFR suspended, AGF no comment on Swiss Re.
newsitem.headline: SAFR suspended, AGF no comment on Swiss Re.

text.p: Trading in shares in French reinsurer Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR) were suspended on Wednesday, pending a statement from the company, a spokesman for the SBF French stock markets association said.
A spokesman for Assurances Generales de France (AGF) declined comment on a Financial Times report it was poised to announce the sale of its 47 percent stake in SAFR to Swiss Reinsurance.
Swiss and German insurance sources told Reuters on January 21 that Swiss Re was talking to AGF to buy its stake in SAFR.
SAFR closed on Tuesday at 1,286 francs.

AGF said on January 13 it had asked British investment bank Schroders to study various options for its SAFR holding, adding that the Athena insurance group which owns 10 percent of SAFR was joining in the review.
Athena is a unit of holding company Worms et Cie.
If Swiss Re bought the AGF and Athena stakes, it would own 78 percent of SAFR, the Financial Times reported.
